namespace Erdos93

/--
If $n$ distinct points in $\mathbb{R}^2$ form a convex polygon then they determine at least
$\lfloor \frac{n}{2}\rfloor$ distinct distances.

Solved by Altman [Al63].
-/
@[category research solved, AMS 52, formal_proof using lean4 at "https://github.com/plby/lean-proofs/blob/1d7b3f00780b85ed0462e79a1cd5650ee9055655/src/v4.29.1/ErdosProblems/Erdos93.lean"]
theorem erdos_93 (A : Finset ℝ²) (hA : ConvexIndep (A : Set ℝ²)) :
    A.card / 2 ≤ distinctDistances A := by
  sorry

end Erdos93

reformulations.difference: The source describes points forming a convex polygon; Lean uses an unordered finite set satisfying ConvexIndep.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: For a finite planar set with at least three elements, requiring every point to lie outside the convex hull of the remaining points says exactly that all points are vertices of their convex hull. Such a set cannot be collinear, and its convex hull is a convex polygon with precisely those vertices. Conversely, every vertex of a convex polygon lies outside the convex hull of its other vertices. The number of distinct distances is independent of the cyclic ordering. The equivalence with Mathlib's set-indexed ConvexIndependent predicate was also checked in Lean, although the full geometric polygon characterization was not formalized in the scratch file.

reformulations.difference: Lean includes cardinalities 0, 1 and 2, whereas a polygon ordinarily has at least three vertices and the linked external theorem explicitly assumes 3 ≤ n.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: For cardinalities 0 and 1, the lower bound is zero. A two-element set determines exactly one positive distance, matching 2 / 2 = 1. Thus the additional cases are automatic. In /workspace/review/scratch.lean, review_equiv_restricted_statement proves equivalence with the external theorem's n ≥ 3 signature, including the ConvexIndependent predicate and filtered-Cartesian-product distance set. Its axiom report contains only propext, Classical.choice and Quot.sound.

review.notes: No mathematical defect found in the sole declaration. The current source records an affirmative solution by Altman and verification in Lean, consistent with both attributes. Checked the genuine Euclidean metric, exclusion of self-distances, deduplication of equal lengths, and natural-number division as floor(n/2). Scratch proofs verify empty/singleton/two-point cases, exclusion of zero from the distance set, and non-vacuity on unit-circle subsets, including a square. The final scratch file compiles successfully. Full texts of Al63, Er90, Er92e, Er97e and Er97f could not be retrieved; their bibliographic records were checked, while the exact website statement and seven accessible primary papers establish faithfulness. The linked proof has the appropriate statement and no explicit sorry or custom axioms. Its original Lean/Mathlib 4.29.1 build was not independently reproduced: compilation against the supplied 4.33.1 environment encountered compatibility errors. This is a verification limitation, not evidence of a statement or status defect.
